text.p: The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) said on Friday that it was continuing to scrutinise trading in Bougainville Copper Ltd but would not comment on a newspaper report which speculated that recent share dealings could be linked to mercenary action on the troubled island.
"The ASX is continuing its normal surveillance examination of trade in Bougainville Copper Ltd," an exchange spokesman said. "But we are unable to make any further comment."
The Sydney Morning Herald said large share dealings in Bougainville Copper in mid-February had aroused the suspicion of Australian government officials.
"Australian officials said it appeared the shares may have been purchased as part of the mercenary deal," the newspaper said in its Friday edition.
"The Papua New Guinea government is paying the company which has provided the mercenary force, Executive Outcomes, A$36 million for its operation in Papua New Guinea," it said.

On February 17, the ASX queried Bougainville Copper, which is a unit of Anglo-Australian mining giant RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd about unusually large turnover and a jump in its share price from 43 cents three days earlier to 61 cents.
The company's daily turnover also rose in that period to a as high of 466,455, ten times larger than normal turnover.
A regulatory source said the ASX had not yet identified the buyer of these shares.
Bougainville Copper's giant Panguna copper mine was shut in May 1989 by seccessionist rebels who have successfully countered all government attempts to end their uprising.
